what.text: Somatropin is recombinant human growth hormone, a protein made to match the hormone the pituitary gland releases. It is given by injection under the skin. It is a protein of 191 amino acids, not a small peptide.

Growth hormone release falls with age. In 1990, a small study proposed that this decline helps explain the loss of lean mass and gain of fat in old age, which led to interest in growth hormone for aging.

src.label: Rudman et al., N Engl J Med, 1990

what.text: Somatropin is FDA approved only for specific medical conditions. Aging is not an approved use, and US federal law makes it a crime to distribute human growth hormone for any unapproved use.

research.text: Randomized trials in healthy older adults, lasting about 6 months, found that growth hormone added lean mass and cut fat, but did not clearly raise strength. It caused swelling, joint pain, carpal tunnel symptoms and more diabetes or glucose intolerance. No trial has shown that it slows aging or extends life.
Each is listed below as it was run.

research.title: Men over 60 (Rudman), 1990

facts.v: Non-randomized comparison: 12 men treated, 9 untreated, after a 6-month baseline
21 healthy men aged 61 to 81 with low IGF-1 levels
6 months of injections three times a week
Lean body mass, fat mass, skin thickness, bone density

research.found: Treated men gained 8.8% lean mass, lost 14.4% fat mass and gained 1.6% spine bone density. Skin thickness changes were not significant, nor were hip or wrist bone changes.

src.label: Rudman et al., N Engl J Med, 1990

research.title: Growth hormone with or without sex hormones, adults 65 to 88, 2002

facts.v: 131 healthy community-dwelling adults aged 65 to 88: 57 women, 74 men
Lean mass, fat mass, strength, fitness (VO2 max), side effects

research.found: Growth hormone increased lean mass and cut fat in both sexes. Strength did not rise significantly, except a borderline gain in men on growth hormone plus testosterone. Diabetes or glucose intolerance occurred in 18 men given growth hormone vs 7 not given it.

research.title: Blood sugar and fats in the 2002 trial, 2009

facts.v: Secondary analysis of the 2002 double-blind, factorial trial
Glucose, insulin, insulin sensitivity, blood fats

research.found: Growth hormone raised insulin resistance in women and men. It lowered LDL cholesterol and raised triglycerides.

src.label: Münzer et al., J Clin Endocrinol Metab, 2009

research.text: A 2007 review of 18 randomized trials in healthy older people (220 given growth hormone, mean age 69) found 2.1 kg less fat and 2.1 kg more lean mass, with no change in weight or bone density. Treated people had more swelling, joint pain, carpal tunnel syndrome and breast growth (gynecomastia), and somewhat more new diabetes. The review notes that growth hormone is not FDA approved for aging.

src.label: Liu et al., Ann Intern Med, 2007 (systematic review, healthy elderly)

research.text: A 2008 review of trials in fit young adults found more lean mass but no clear gain in strength or exercise capacity, and more swelling and fatigue.

src.label: Liu et al., Ann Intern Med, 2008 (systematic review, athletes)

us.text: Somatropin is FDA approved, by prescription, under many brand names for growth hormone deficiency and some other conditions. No brand is approved for aging. Distributing human growth hormone for any use other than an FDA-authorized use, on a doctor's order, is a federal crime. As of November 1, 2026.

items.text: FDA's data list somatropin products including Genotropin (1995), Humatrope, Norditropin, Nutropin, Omnitrope, Saizen, Zomacton, Serostim and Zorbtive. They are licensed as biologics (BLAs).
children with growth failure from growth hormone deficiency, Prader-Willi syndrome, small for gestational age, Turner syndrome or idiopathic short stature; and adults with growth hormone deficiency.
adults with HIV and wasting or cachexia, together with antiretroviral therapy.

knowingly distributing, or possessing with intent to distribute, human growth hormone for any human use other than treating a disease or recognized medical condition authorized by FDA, on a physician's order, is punishable by up to 5 years in prison (10 years if a person under 18 is involved). The law covers somatropin, somatrem and their analogues, and lets the DEA investigate.

world.lead: Somatropin is an approved prescription medicine in the US, the EU, the UK and Canada, and a prescription-only medicine in Australia with extra possession controls. No regulator we checked has approved it for aging. WADA prohibits growth hormone at all times.

countries.status: Approved biologic under many brands (e.g. Genotropin) for growth disorders, adult GH deficiency and HIV wasting. Distribution for unapproved uses is a crime.

after.title: Sport
after.text: Growth hormone is prohibited at all times (in and out of competition) under S2.2.3 of the 2026 WADA Prohibited List, with its analogues and fragments. It is a non-Specified Substance. The 2027 list keeps the same wording.

side.text: Somatropin can cause fluid retention, joint and muscle pain, carpal tunnel syndrome and high blood sugar. The label warns of deaths in critically ill patients and in some children with Prader-Willi syndrome, and of tumor growth. In healthy older adults it raised the rate of diabetes or glucose intolerance.

items.text: increased deaths have been reported in people with acute critical illness after heart or abdominal surgery, major trauma or acute respiratory failure.
deaths have been reported after starting treatment in children with severe obesity, airway obstruction, sleep apnea or respiratory infection.
monitor existing tumors for growth; childhood cancer survivors have a higher risk of a second tumor, especially meningioma after head radiation.
it may unmask glucose intolerance or diabetes. In older adults, diabetes or glucose intolerance occurred in 18 men on growth hormone vs 7 not on it.
swelling, joint pain, muscle pain and carpal tunnel syndrome, especially in adults. In the 2002 trial, swelling affected 39% of women on growth hormone and joint pain 41% of men.
raised pressure in the skull, severe allergic reactions, low cortisol, low thyroid, slipped hip growth plates and worsening scoliosis in children, and pancreatitis.
the label has no human fertility data. In rats, very high doses (about 24 times the human dose) caused fewer and less motile sperm in males, irregular cycles in females, and lower pregnancy rates.
gynecomastia was more common with growth hormone in trials of healthy older people.

surprises: Growth hormone has its own criminal law: 21 U.S.C. 333(e) makes distributing it for any use FDA has not authorized a felony, with up to 5 years in prison, so off-label anti-aging distribution is itself a crime.
Australia lists somatropin in Appendix D of its Poisons Standard, making possession without authority illegal.
In healthy older adults, growth hormone added lean mass but did not clearly raise strength, and raised diabetes or glucose intolerance.
